title: Karaage Crispy Japanese Fried Chicken

seo.title: Karaage Recipe: Crispy Japanese Fried Chicken
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of crispy Karaage with our authentic Japanese fried chicken recipe. Learn how to make perfectly juicy and flavorful Karaage at home with ease!

h2Headings: How to Make Karaage: Step-by-Step Instructions

seo.imageCaption: Our Karaage recipe guarantees perfectly crispy, juicy Japanese fried chicken every time!

description: Karaage is a beloved Japanese fried chicken, renowned for its incredibly juicy interior and irresistibly crispy coating. This classic dish is marinated in a savory blend of soy sauce, ginger, and garlic, then lightly coated and deep-fried to golden perfection. It's a delightful treat perfect as an appetizer, snack, or main course, offering a burst of umami with every bite.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken and Marinade
instructions.text: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. In a large bowl, combine soy sauce, sake, mirin, grated ginger, grated garlic, and sesame oil. Add the chicken pieces, ensuring they are well coated. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 1-2 hours in the refrigerator for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Coating
instructions.text: In a separate shallow bowl, whisk the egg into the marinated chicken. In another shallow bowl, combine potato starch, all-purpose flour, and black pepper. Mix well to ensure an even coating blend.

instructions.title: Coat the Chicken
instructions.text: Take each piece of marinated chicken and dredge it thoroughly in the starch-flour mixture, pressing gently to ensure a good, even coat. Shake off any excess coating. Place the coated chicken on a wire rack or plate, ensuring pieces are not touching, to allow the coating to set slightly.

instructions.title: Heat the Oil
instructions.text: Pour vegetable or canola oil into a deep pot or Dutch oven, ensuring it is at least 5-7 cm deep. Heat the oil over medium-high heat to 170°C (340°F). Use a kitchen thermometer for accuracy.

instructions.title: First Fry
instructions.text: Carefully add a batch of chicken pieces to the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for about 3-4 minutes until lightly golden and cooked through. Remove the chicken with a slotted spoon or spider and place it on a wire rack to drain excess oil. Repeat with remaining chicken.

instructions.title: Second Fry for Crispy Texture
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 180°C (355°F). Return the chicken to the hot oil in batches for a second fry, about 1-2 minutes, until deeply golden brown and extra crispy. This double-frying technique is key for ultimate crispiness.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Remove the perfectly crispy Karaage from the oil and drain on a clean wire rack or paper towels. Serve hot with fresh lemon wedges and a side of Japanese mayonnaise for dipping. Enjoy your homemade, authentic Karaage!

tips: For the crispiest Karaage, double-frying is crucial. The first fry cooks the chicken through, and the second, at a higher temperature, creates an incredibly crunchy exterior.
Potato starch (katakuriko) is traditional for Karaage and gives a lighter, crispier coating than cornstarch, though cornstarch can be used as a substitute.
Serve Karaage immediately for the best texture. If reheating, use an air fryer or oven to regain crispiness, avoiding the microwave.
